summary: This program stores three shopping-cart items in variables and joins them into one readable line using the + operator, then prints the result.

lines.text: Each item is a string value held in its own variable, so the text lives in one place and the joining logic below can refer to it by name.

The + operator on strings means concatenation, not addition: it glues the pieces together end to end. The ", " in between is a literal separator, and the space inside the quotes is what keeps the items from running together.
Building the sentence with concatenation lets you reuse cart_list wherever it is needed, rather than repeating the three item names in the print call.
